d0e6bfb03a.why: Re-asks a T1 fact under a T3 name. The key (the rock around a fossil began as soft mud or sand that later hardened) and its lava lure are rock-layers-and-fossils (T1) keys put together: 51ee2d2282 (fossils lie in rock built from sand and mud, not rock that cooled from lava, with the same lava lure), 9237791b44 (mud and sand bury the remains) and 0263ee3155 (sand and mud harden into rock over time). A 5th-grade graduate answers it knowing nothing of Steno, and the tier rule tests the fact, not the framing; the grade_note itself names the fact as 'a fossil lies in rock that began as soft sediment'. This is the same pattern the lead's ruling forbids for superposition (Steno as the person, not the earlier fact again). Second, smaller: the stem already calls the stone 'such a tooth', which rules out 'the stone slowly grew' in solid rock. The facts themselves check out (UCMP: 'buried in soft sediments which hardened later'; a stone grown in rock 'would have been distorted'). No one-phrase fix: rekey on what Steno added, for instance what he concluded the tongue stones were (teeth of sharks that once lived) without the shark dissection in the stem, or drop it.
